quest.title: The Forest and the Princess
quest.description: In the forest, a princess is preparing to go solve a certain problem herself...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.text: Your Highness! What brings you here?
...Given how things stand, I shall retrieve the <color=#00E1FFFF>relic</color> myself, and then decide what to do next.
Your Highness! That will not do!
Your Highness! You cannot go!
Oh? It seems you have a better solution. Let's hear it then, Minister Saborn.

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: I... Uh... Would like to inform Your Highness that, following a long discussion with Souffache last night, we have come to the conclusion that... It would be better to set up a trial ground elsewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: Hear, hear! And then the Guardian who passes our selection process can retrieve the relic for us — two birds, one stone!

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: But without the relic, how can we be sure that the chosen Guardian is really the one we are looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Worry not, ministers. Though we are indeed facing a great crisis, this is precisely as the legends predicted.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: When the crisis befalls us, a Guardian shall thereupon emerge. At this moment, what I must do is ensure that they are shown the right path.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Besides, I am the best flyer in the kingdom, so there is none more suitable than I to judge the Guardian's abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Then will you go instead?

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: I—I'm afraid... My legs are rather useless when it comes to flight of any kind...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: How about you, Saborn? Will you go?

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: Uhh, m—my eyesight... Alas, I fear I would be unable to see their movements clearly enough to judge...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Good, that's settled then. The two of you will stay to handle affairs within the kingdom, while I shall assist in managing the selection process at the original location myself.

choices.text: Something fun going on?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Oh, greetings to both of you, and welcome to the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells. You're very welcome to sign up for the "Guardian of the Kingdom" selection trials.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You have not previously participated in the selection trials of our Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, if I am not mistaken?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How does Your Highness know this?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Your appearance differs greatly from our kingdom's subjects. Had you taken part before, I would not forget it.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Oh! That's enough chit-chat, I suppose. As it so happens, I was just about to head over to host the selection ceremony near the Relic Shrine. Let us go there together.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Ministers, the kingdom's affairs are in your hands. Do try not to let anyone cut this tree down while I'm away finding our true Guardian, if you could?

response.speaker: Saborn & Souffache
response.text: *sigh* As you wish, Your Highness.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: The two of you, please come with me. Before the selection officially begins, there are a few things I still need to tell you.

choices.text: Might I submit myself as a candidate for the trial, Your Highness?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, ooh! We're good at flying, and adventuring too! Can we participate?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Please wait here a moment. I will introduce the trial for you, as well as a few things that you'll need to watch out for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Her Highness sure is a decisive decision-maker, huh? Guess that's a true princess for you...

choices.text: I declared I'd accept the trial quite suddenly...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hmm? Oh... Perhaps my introduction seemed a little too forthcoming. My apologies.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: In truth, there have been many squirrels who — like you — have suddenly turned up and declared their intention to undergo the trial, so I am already accustomed to receiving such "candidates."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: At least... There were many, before that dragon attacked the kingdom.

choices.text: You said it was to retrieve a relic...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It is indeed. As I mentioned, not long ago, a giant dragon passed through our kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: We tried our best to drive it away, but before leaving, it trampled both the trial ground and the sacred site where the relic was kept to smithereens.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Our original, stable trial environment is now very different from the way it used to be. The wind currents have become unpredictable, causing a dramatic increase in the difficulty of some trial stages.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After the environment changed so drastically, some candidates — who could have easily passed the first few stages before — now find even the very first stage too challenging.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But from another perspective, the current trial is actually a better test of a candidate's true strength, so it should better help us choose a strong "Guardian of the Kingdom."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I—I'm pretty strong!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon too!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hmm... Well if that is truly the case, let us get straight to it. Allow me to introduce the trial for you.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Simply put, in this trial, the candidate must help their squirrel companion fly in the right direction by guiding them along the wind currents.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Don't worry, it isn't complicated. All you have to do is observe the direction of the currents and make decisions accordingly.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Of course, you need not worry about the issue of direction. In this kingdom, no wind can stop me from flying wherever I will.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Alright, let us begin. Please make sure you're both ready.

choices.text: Is it being kept somewhere dangerous?
But Your Highness didn't seem particularly surprised...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your Highness, you're amazing! You flew past so easily!

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Your ability to judge the wind's currents was also remarkable. It seems you are worthy to undergo the trial after all.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Let us make haste to the site where the relic is being kept... Hopefully we won't have another run-in with that dragon.
"...I am a voice, but not life..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh, what was that? It sounded like... someone's voice? {NICKNAME}, did you hear that?

choices.text: I definitely heard it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, The Princess is way ahead... Let's forget about that for now and catch up with her first.

choices.text: ...But I have no idea what it meant.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: *sigh* When will I be able to find a Guardian...

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: If we cannot find one, then at the very least we must allow Her Highness to...

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: ...I've heard that in Brickstacks, they have a way to go outside the world, otherwise...

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: Saborn, that's quite enough. As for the exact method, we can discuss the details later...

talks.objective: Undergo the trial with Princess Cimest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... This is where the relic was being kept?

choices.text: These footprints are massive.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Perhaps in driving the dragon away, we also drove it into a rage.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: The relic is down there. Pass the trial, and you may claim it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thought that the relic would be protected by some kind of seal, or guard, or... something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But it looks like it's just lying there, and it doesn't seem like anything's stopping someone from just taking it...

choices.text: Just a hop and a step away.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: What you say is correct. This relic does indeed have a "seal" — namely, the "trial" that you have seen.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: According to the kingdom's records, one must pass the trial in order to retrieve the relic.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Conversely, if it is taken by someone who has not yet passed the trial, it will lose its "meaning" as a relic.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Thus, even I must pass the entire trial to retrieve the "true" relic.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: There must be both a "trial" and a "challenger" to do so.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Without satisfying these two conditions, the best-case scenario is that we'd be walking away with a useless lump of stone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The best-case scenario"... Does that mean something worse could happen, too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Those who act in defiance of the rules shall be cursed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C—Cursed! Uhh, in that case, let's just... go ahead and accept the trial...

choices.text: Why don't we just jump down and take it?
That dragon must be huge...

talks.objective: Undergo the trial with Princess Cimest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #We passed! {NICKNAME}, we're Guardians now! So is this the relic that's used to acknowledge new Guardians?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There's something carved onto it, like a line of text maybe? Let Paimon take a closer look...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uhh, Paimon doesn't get it. Do you get it, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: It's probably some roundabout way of cheering us on?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Those words have always been there. Even I do not know their origin...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: I sense that they may hold some great significance for the kingdom... But I have yet to grasp their meaning.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Whatever the case, given your performance in the trial, you are undoubtedly the most suitable candidate for the title of "Guardian" that I've ever met.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Your abilities and judgment are beyond question. Meeting you at a time like this is truly a blessing for our kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now that we have retrieved the relic, we may hold the ceremony right away.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: I am fully confident that your courage and abilities will have won you the relic's respect.

choices.text: You flatter me, Your Highness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, it was nothing! We're just glad we could help you, Your Highness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! When did you guys get here? Paimon didn't even notice you arrive!

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: We flew over, of course! We were among the best flyers around when we were young, you know. How else would we have been able to serve the princess?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Never judge a squirrel by its appearance...

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: Well, I never! A visitor turning up at our time of crisis, a Guardian emerging from the trials victorious... and the relic in our possession, intact and unharmed!

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: Your Highness, everything is exactly as the legends said!

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: It seems that our kingdom finally has a "future" to look forward to!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: We shall find out soon enough.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now, please place your hand upon the relic. Let it light up and proclaim that you are henceforth the "Guardian of the Kingdom"!

choices.text: ...Erm, do... do you think it's not bright enough?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon take a look... Ehh? M—Maybe it's been there so long that... it just can't light up anymore?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kinda like how candles that've been lying around too long won't burn very brightly.

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: How... How could that be? All the details match, yet the relic still...

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: Your Highness, whatever the case, at least the relic is in our hands. Even if our guest has failed to be acknowledged by...

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: Your Highness?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Set the relic aside. It is my kingdom for which the challengers have come; therefore it is I who must acknowledge them.

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: Your Highness! B—But no ruler of our kingdom has ever taken it upon themselves to acknowledge a "Guardian"...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Then let us create a precedent for future rulers to follow.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come forward.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: As Princess of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, I hereby declare...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: #That {NICKNAME} and Paimon shall henceforth be recognized as the kingdom's "Paladins of Breezes and Bells"!

choices.text: At your service, Your Highness.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hooray! A "Paladin of Breezes and Bells"... Hehe, such a cool title!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Definitely cooler than just being any old guardian.

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: B—But surely that means we still haven't found our "Guardian"? And if that is so, then we won't be able to fulfill our "calling."

response.speaker: Souffache
response.text: And if we cannot fulfill our "calling"... We'll no longer have a "future" to look forward to, just like the kingdoms that came before us...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Fret not, I will find a way.

choices.text: You have my sword.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: My thanks, good Paladin. I will indeed need your help.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But first, I will need to put the pieces of this puzzle together...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After some time has passed, please return to my kingdom to meet me. When the time is nigh, we shall set forth in search of the kingdom's future together.

choices.text: Shouldst thou require my aid, I am at thy service.
It is my honor, Your Highness.
Has... it even lit up at all?
Nothing can stand in our way!
It's probably meant to encourage challengers.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: ...I didn't expect you to be able to judge the wind currents so accurately.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: If you were flying squirrels like I am, navigating those wind currents would pose you no challenge, of that I am certain...

choices.text: Paimon's a natural when it comes to flying.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Pfff... Is that so? I'm glad to hear that, because you two are the most Guardian-like candidates I've ever seen.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Then let us continue. The current wind conditions are just right.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No problem!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, everything's going great! Maybe we're the Guardians that Her Highness has been looking for.

choices.text: Your Highness was outstanding, too.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Thank you for your kind words. I had in fact passed the trial many times before the dragon destroyed the sacred site.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Purely in terms of flying ability, I am confident that no other squirrel is my equal. Previous candidates found even the first few stages too difficult.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But if Your Highness already passed the trial, how come you didn't take the relic?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Unfortunately, the relic has yet to acknowledge me.

choices.text: So even Guardians require the relic's acknowledgment?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: That I do not know. Perhaps it thought I didn't pass the trial...

choices.text: Surely there aren't hidden stages?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: All I know is, the relic has never lit up for me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But you... Not only have you come precisely at our kingdom's hour of need, but your capabilities are undeniable. That is why I believe you will earn the relic's acknowledgement.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Let us continue. The final stage of the trial awaits.

choices.text: Do the trial stages change for each challenger?
Why does that relic get to call all the shots...
Your Highness is the only true Guardian.
If everyone had to use wind gliders, I'd be unbeatable.

talks.objective: Undergo the trial with Princess Cimest

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That dragon is actually...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell the story of the dragon to Princess Cimest in its entirety, sparing no detail...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Can such a thing be? Truly unexpected.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: At the time, I was too panicked, and so I just gave the order to drive him away.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Had we the chance to calmly speak with one another, perhaps...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Ahem! Never mind. What's done is done. We must focus on the problem at hand.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: As for that dragon... once all our problems have been resolved, I shall visit him personally.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now, let us focus on the relic.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: The relic is down there. Pass the trial, and you may claim it.

choices.text: Wait, speaking of choosing a Guardian...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean that Faurobert who could jump super high?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right! The whole reason they held that contest was to find a champion to come rescue the princess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although it doesn't seem like the princess needs saving. If you were looking for a super-strong champion to win your contest, they just so happen to have one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In fact, there's bound to be heaps of potential champions over there!

choices.text: Wait... By "contest," you mean "trial."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: What an extraordinary coincidence...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Though our trial doesn't really have anything to do with jumping. Still, from what you've said, it sounds like they've found the strongest candidate to complete their calling.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...It seems a trip over to Rainsong Pond is in order. Thank you for informing me.

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: Wait! But Your Highness, they're all paper frogs over there! They're nothing like us, they're not...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: So what? A Guardian's most vital asset is what is in their heart, not their appearance.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Ministers, you are to stay and look after the kingdom while I am gone. I will go to Rainsong Pond myself.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: My loyal Paladin, I hope that the "Champion" over at Rainsong Pond is as fearless and skilled as you are.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Skilled is certainly accurate...

choices.text: But as for fearless...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Oh? You mean to say that this "Champion" of theirs is actually... a sheep in wolf's clothing?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hahaha! Then all the more reason to go meet him in person!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Alright, that's settled then. Oh, and if I'm going over to Rainsong Pond... Perhaps I'd better bring some gifts...
